I'll think this through like the farmer would, then give the plan.

---

My land is 4.1 mu, not much. Me and my wife, two mouths. I've been doing this wheat-then-maize thing for 35 years. Last year was alright, wheat gave me around 450 kg per mu, maize close to 550 kg per mu. I'll do about the same as last year. No reason to change what works.

**Wheat (winter, October planting):**

I buy seed from the dealer in town — improved variety, the one most neighbors plant. Costs a bit more than saving my own, but the yield is better. I use about 15 kg seed per mu because our soil here is heavy and I want a thick stand.

For base fertilizer before sowing, I spread 2 bags of diammonium (50 kg bag) across my 4.1 mu. That works out to about 24 kg per mu of the compound. Then in spring when the wheat wakes up (March, jointing time), I put down urea — one bag (50 kg) over the whole field, so maybe 12 kg per mu. I give it water at that time too, pumped from my well. Another watering before the grain fills in May.

Total nitrogen on wheat: the diammonium has about 18% N, so 24 × 0.18 ≈ 4.3 kg N, plus urea 12 × 0.46 ≈ 5.5 kg. Plus I throw a half bag of urea at sowing too. Call it around 14 kg N per mu. Phosphorus from diammonium about 11 kg per mu. Potassium I don't buy separately — too expensive and my soil has some.

Spray for weeds once in spring, and one spray for aphids and disease around heading time. Two sprays total. I plough before sowing — the soil needs turning after maize stubble.

**Maize (summer, June right after wheat harvest):**

I plant hybrid seed, everybody does — you can't save maize seed and get anything. One bag covers my field. I drill it in right after wheat combine, no tillage, just straight into the stubble. Saves time and water.

Base fertilizer at planting: one bag of compound (15-15-15), about 12 kg per mu. Then at big trumpet stage (July), I topdress urea — 15 kg per mu. Maize eats a lot of nitrogen. Total N maybe 18-19 kg per mu. I water once after planting to get it up, once more in July if no rain. The summer rains usually come.

One spray for corn borer, maybe one for weeds early. Two sprays.

I don't waste money on things I don't need, but I won't be stingy on fertilizer — if the crop is short, that's real loss. Better a little extra than not enough.
